reason: The text narrates Yahweh's direct intervention to save the Hebrew people from death at the hands of the pursuing Egyptian army. Key evidence includes: (1) Moses declares to the fearful Israelites 'stand firm and see the salvation of Yahweh (יְשׁוּעַ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה) which He will do for you today'; (2) God promises 'Yahweh will fight for you (יְהוָ֖ה יִלָּחֵ֣ם לָכֶ֑ם)'; (3) the divine agent (angel of God and pillar of cloud) actively positions itself to protect Israel; (4) Yahweh causes the sea to return to normal, drowning the Egyptian army and simultaneously delivering Israel to safety; and (5) the passage explicitly states 'Yahweh saved Israel (וַיּוֹשַׁע יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל) on that day from the hand of the Egyptians.' The entire passage demonstrates Yahweh's active commitment to the physical safety and deliverance of the Hebrew people.
